pages.title: Thermal Heater
pages.text: A fuel-burning heater. Inside a sealed room it heats the air, which warms the walls and floor. Larger rooms warm more slowly; insulation reduces heat loss. Open camps retain nearby warmth. Right-click with coal, charcoal, blaze powder, coal blocks, or cryo fuel to activate.$(br2)Essential for early survival. Place these in your base to keep temperatures livable through Phases 2-4. Multiple heaters add power. After burnout, stored room warmth cools gradually.$(br2)Can be $(l:heating/heater_upgrades)upgraded$(/l) with iron, gold, or diamond for greater output.$(br2)$(italic)ORSA FAQ: "Can I hug the heater?" No. "Can I sleep next to the heater?" Also no. "Can I name the heater?" ...we can't stop you, but please seek companionship elsewhere.$()
Surround a Thermal Core with 8 iron ingots. It's essentially an iron box with a hot thing inside. ORSA charged the UN four billion credits for this design.

pages.title: Air and Structure
pages.text: Air holds little heat; walls hold much more. A vacuum breach vents the air while surviving walls retain warmth. Repair the seal and restore oxygen: incoming cold air warms from those walls.$(br2)Without room air, heaters keep burning but heat the structure at reduced efficiency. Radiation supplies only part of that warmth to you; EVA and oxygen still matter.$(br2)Wool and snow insulate well. Wood is better than stone; glass, metal and ice lose heat readily. Layers up to three blocks thick combine their insulation.$(br2)Each heater automatically targets 20°C. Heaters in the same room share demand: extra heaters speed up warm-up, then throttle together. The status panel shows a short average of burn percentage and estimated fuel time. The estimate changes while walls warm or room conditions change.$(br2)Redstone stops heating and holds your fuel. Stored warmth still cools naturally. Better insulation lowers the fuel needed to hold the target; frostmites and industrial machinery can add separate fuel costs.$(br2)Use an $(l:heating/thermostat)ORSA Thermostat$(/l) to choose a sensed target from 10-30°C and account for local Core warmth.
